payload.rationale: Annual headline inflation is running at 3.4% as of August 2026, with August core CPI at 0.3% and headline at 0.4%. The FOMC projects 2026 PCE inflation at 3.7%. These figures suggest an average monthly inflation rate of around 0.25% to 0.3%. Therefore, a November reading of 0.3% or higher (>0.2%) is more likely than not. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that energy prices often decline in the late fall, which could drag headline CPI down to 0.2% or lower, similar to the low prints seen in June (-0.4%) and July (0.1%). The strongest reason this estimate could be too low is that the underlying core inflation trend remains robust at 0.3%, and any positive contribution from volatile components like energy or food would easily push the headline index to 0.3% or higher.
limitations: October and November price data are not observed. No current commodity-price forecast or complete CPI component model is supplied.
PCE is a different index from CPI; annual inflation is not monthly inflation. Strict threshold and one-decimal rounding matter.
